answer_1.quote: We show that real world images can be automatically matched to captions to generate false but compelling news stories, a threat scenario that may lead to larger-scale image repurposing.
answer_1.outputs: false but compelling news stories by matching real images to out-of-context captions

answer_2.quote: We report classification accuracy over all samples (All) and separately for the Pristine and Falsified samples. We also report model performance at varying false alarm rates via ROC curves.

answer_4.quote: We conduct our evaluation on Amazon Mechanical Turk. For each image-caption pair we ask 5 workers the following three questions: (a) "Could this image belong to the given caption?" (Yes/No), (b) "How confident are you in your answer?" (1: Very, 2: Somewhat, 3: Not at all), (c) "Would it help to use a search engine to be more confident?" (Yes/No).
answer_4.guideline: Workers were asked whether the image could belong to the caption, their confidence level, and whether a search engine would help. They were instructed not to use search engines.
